faq_items.question: How do working moms keep their house clean?
faq_items.answer: Working moms keep a house clean by shrinking daily cleaning to a 15-minute reset and assigning just one focus zone per weekday instead of one big weekend clean. Anchoring the reset to an existing habit, like after dinner, keeps it running on autopilot rather than willpower.

faq_items.question: How much time do working moms need to clean each day?
faq_items.answer: About 15 minutes on weekdays, plus one 15-to-25-minute focus zone. That is roughly 30 to 40 minutes a day spread across the week — around 3 to 4 hours total — instead of losing an entire weekend day to catch-up cleaning.

faq_items.question: What is a realistic cleaning schedule when you work full-time?
faq_items.answer: A realistic full-time schedule assigns one zone per day: floors Monday, bathrooms Tuesday, dusting Wednesday, kitchen Thursday, laundry Friday, bedrooms Saturday, and a reset Sunday. Each day stays light enough to finish after work, and a missed day just resumes at the next zone.

faq_items.question: How do I get my kids and partner to help with cleaning?
faq_items.answer: Assign specific, named tasks to specific people and post the plan where everyone sees it, like the fridge. Match chores to age so they are doable without supervision, and add a visible check-off so the mental load of tracking everything stops landing on you.

faq_items.question: How do you stick to a cleaning schedule with an unpredictable work week?
faq_items.answer: Treat the schedule as a flexible guide, not a pass-fail test. When a busy day blows up a zone, skip it and pick up the next day's — never restart the whole week. Checking off four of seven days still leaves your home far cleaner than an all-or-nothing plan.
